clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Policy. It is the policy of my Administration that all students 
should be guaranteed an educational environment free from discrimination 
on the basis of sex, including discrimination in the form of sexual harassment, 
which encompasses sexual violence, and including discrimination on the 
basis of sexual orientation or gender identity. For students attending schools 
and other educational institutions that receive Federal financial assistance, 
this guarantee is codified, in part, in Title IX of the Education Amendments 
of 1972, 20 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., which prohibits discrimination on the 
basis of sex in education programs or activities receiving Federal financial 
assistance.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Review of Agency Actions. (a) Within 100 days of the date of this 
order, the Secretary of Education, in consultation with the Attorney General, 
shall review all existing regulations, orders, guidance documents, policies, 
and any other similar agency actions (collectively, agency actions) that are 
or may be inconsistent with the policy set forth in section 1 of this order, 
and provide the findings of this review to the Director of the Office of 
Management and Budget.

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text:
(i) As part of the review required under subsection (a) of this section, 
the Secretary of Education shall review the rule entitled ‘‘Nondiscrimina-
tion on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving 
Federal Financial Assistance,’’ 85 FR 30026 (May 19, 2020), and any 
other agency actions taken pursuant to that rule, for consistency with 
governing law, including Title IX, and with the policy set forth in section 
1 of this order.

clauses.label: (ii)
clauses.text:
(ii) As soon as practicable, and as appropriate and consistent with applica-
ble law, the Secretary of Education shall review existing guidance and 
issue new guidance as needed on the implementation of the rule described 
in subsection (a)(i) of this section, for consistency with governing law, 
including Title IX, and with the policy set forth in section 1 of this 
order.

clauses.label: (iii)
clauses.text:
(iii) The Secretary of Education shall consider suspending, revising, or 
rescinding—or publishing for notice and comment proposed rules sus-
pending, revising, or rescinding—those agency actions that are inconsistent 
with the policy set forth in section 1 of this order as soon as practicable 
and as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, and may issue 
such requests for information as would facilitate doing so.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Secretary of Education shall consider taking additional enforcement 
actions, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, to enforce the 
policy set forth in section 1 of this order as well as legal prohibitions 
on sex discrimination in the form of sexual harassment, which encompasses 
sexual violence, to the fullest extent permissible under law; to account 
for intersecting forms of prohibited discrimination that can affect the avail-
ability of resources and support for students who have experienced sex 
discrimination, including discrimination on the basis of race, disability, 
and national origin; to account for the significant rates at which students

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held registered text of Executive Order 14021 is the official Federal Register text layer at 86 FR 13803, PDF pages 1-2 (Federal Register / Vol. 86, No. 46 / Thursday, March 11, 2021); it names Executive Order 14021 of March 8, 2021, Guaranteeing an Educational Environment Free From Discrimination on the Basis of Sex, Including Sexual Orientation or Gender Identity, and runs from the title to the signature block. The complete clause inventory was checked against the numbered section headings of that text. Section 2(cc) of Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025 (Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions, 90 FR 8237, Federal Register of January 28, 2025) lists Executive Order 14021 of March 8, 2021 among the executive actions that section 2 declares hereby revoked. The held text of Executive Order 14148 states no effective date later than its signing, so the revocation operates from its signing date, 2025-01-20. Whole-order revocation by name is the first end of every clause that had not already been exhausted by performance. The order has no other ending instrument before 2025-01-20 in the packet's later-event chain, which for this order lists besides Executive Order 14148: Executive Order 14168. Each such instrument is recorded in the source notes with its date and why it is not an earlier end; none reinstates this order. The packet's name search of held order texts for this order's number returned, among texts dated on or after 2025-01-20, only Executive Order 14148 and Executive Order 14168. The later-source search is recorded by the three machine searches selected on the sheet: the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09), the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with the CFR bulk files, and the Federal Register executive-order disposition catalog; their coverage statements were read and each is marked complete. Savings are addressed in the savings statement. The first end of the whole order is 2025-01-20.

The held own text of Executive Order 14021 contains no provision that terminates or sets an expiry date for the order or for any clause; deadlines in clauses are performance dates, not ends. No earlier revocation, supersession or amendment that ends a clause is shown in the packet's later-event chain; the instruments it lists other than Executive Order 14148 are addressed in the clause reasons and source notes.","independent_command_check":"Every clause recorded for Executive Order 14021 is a statement or command of that order itself. Statutes, regulations and other instruments that the order cites keep whatever force they have independently of it, but they are not clauses of the order, so no independent command keeps any clause running after the revocation.","savings_check":"Savings were examined in the order's own text and in Executive Order 14148: section 2 contains no saving clause for the revoked orders, section 3(b) leaves existing actions to later review, and section 4 saves only statutory authority and Office of Management and Budget functions. The state is transferred_or_accrued for actions already taken, with no specific surviving action identified from held sources.","scope_check":"Section 2 of Executive Order 14148 revokes the order as a whole by number and by title, without limiting words and without excepting any clause, so the ending is not confined to part of the order. Section 4(a) of Executive Order 14148 states that nothing in it impairs the authority granted by law to an agency or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget; that preserves statutory authority and does not preserve any clause of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: Section 3(b) of Executive Order 14148 directs the Director of the Domestic Policy Council and the Director of the National Economic Council to review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders, memoranda and proclamations listed in section 2 and to take necessary steps to rescind, replace or amend such actions as appropriate. Because rescission of actions already taken is left to later action, Federal actions already taken under Executive Order 14021 before 2025-01-20 were not themselves revoked by section 2 and stood until rescinded, replaced or amended individually. No held source identifies a particular surviving action or its later fate, so none is asserted.
